resources.string: Test your knowledge in Python, Cybersecurity, and C#.
Practice programming and security concepts. Take a Python quiz, review study topics, or check your quiz history.
Five questions: 2 beginner, 2 intermediate, and 1 advanced.
Great practice! Return to the main screen to study or try again.
Choose a topic to view introductory study notes.

BEGINNER
• print() displays text or values in the console. Example: print("Hello")
• bool is the data type for True and False.

INTERMEDIATE
• List slicing uses [start:stop] and excludes the stop index. Example: [10, 20, 30, 40][1:3] gives [20, 30].
• enumerate() provides an index and value while looping through a sequence.

ADVANCED
• A generator produces values as it is iterated. After you fully consume a generator, it is exhausted. Calling list() on that same exhausted generator returns an empty list.

• Confidentiality: protect information from unauthorized access.

• Integrity: protect data from unauthorized changes.

• Availability: keep systems and information accessible when needed.

• Multi-factor authentication (MFA): use more than one authentication factor.

• Phishing: deceptive communication intended to steal data or trick users into unsafe actions.

• Least privilege: give users and programs only the access they need.

• C# is a strongly typed programming language commonly used with .NET.

• Console.WriteLine("Hello"); writes a line to the console.

• int stores whole numbers; string stores text; bool stores true or false.

• A class defines a type, and an object is an instance of a class.

• Methods organize reusable actions.

• Exception handling uses try, catch, and finally blocks.
